documents.title: AI in Academics
documents.summary: The Faculty Resource Center page gives instructors sample syllabus statements for permitting, limiting or (not recommended) prohibiting AI, and a five-level AI-Integrated Assessment Scale with strategies and Canvas indicators. It sets no campus rule and leaves each instructor to choose.
documents.stance_why: The page hands the decision to instructors: it gives syllabus templates for embracing, limiting or prohibiting AI and an 'AI-Integrated Assessment Scale' with 5 levels. It sets no rule of its own, so the stance is delegates with the tiers listed.

units.why: The page justifies its guidance by the worry that "It can be challenging to detect the use of this when students submit their work"; this states a limit on control, so P82 fits and the modality is informs.
units.anchor: It can be challenging to detect the use of this when students submit their work.

units.why: The caveat says "Anything generated by AI can be considered to have been plagiarized"; it classifies AI content as potentially plagiarism (P36), though as a caution to instructors rather than a rule.
units.anchor: Anything generated by AI can be considered to have been plagiarized
units.fit_note: A caveat to instructors that AI output can be viewed as plagiarism, not a stated sanction.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this. The sentence 'Anything generated by AI can be considered to have been plagiarized' is a statement in the source that AI output may count as plagiarism, which is a real policy statement (P36). A had folded it into the caution unit; the two are separate sentences, so it is kept as its own unit. It is a caveat to instructors, so informs; B's fit note kept.

units.why: The line "Caution is urged with what you allow students to use from generative AI" tells instructors to be careful about which AI uses they permit, which leaves the choice to them, so P04 (instructors decide); it is advice, not a rule on students.
units.anchor: Caution is urged with what you allow students to use from generative AI.
units.policy: Caution is urged with what instructors allow students to use from generative AI.
units.fit_note: Advises caution about what to allow rather than stating that each instructor sets the rule.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on policy_type: A P36, B P04; unit_stance: A restrict, B neutral. A merged the plagiarism caveat and the caution sentence into one P36 unit; B coded them as two units, the caution under P04. The source has two separate sentences: 'Anything generated by AI can be considered to have been plagiarized' and 'Caution is urged with what you allow students to use'. The caution sentence is advice to instructors about what they allow, so the instructor-decides type P04 fits; the plagiarism caveat is coded as its own P36 unit (B-only, kept). Stance restrict because the advice leans toward limiting what is allowed. Final: actor instructor, phase before-course, modality should, policy_type P04, unit_stance restrict. (Coder A's fit_note on P36: Frames AI output as possible plagiarism and advises caution to instructors, but does not itself classify student use as misconduct.)

units.why: The template note says to "Adjust this statement to reflect your particular parameters of acceptable use", so each instructor sets the rule: P04.
units.anchor: Adjust this statement to reflect your particular parameters of acceptable use
units.frag_start: This syllabus statement is useful when
units.policy: Instructors adjust the sample statement to the AI uses they find acceptable in their own course.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this. 'Adjust this statement to reflect your particular parameters of acceptable use' tells instructors that the sample statement is theirs to change, so each instructor sets the rule (P04). A coded the sample statement's content but not this instruction. Kept.

units.why: The sample statement permits "Brainstorming and refining your ideas" in a course allowing some uses, which is a permission for idea generation, so P15.
units.anchor: Brainstorming and refining your ideas
units.policy: The use of generative AI tools is permitted in this course for brainstorming and refining your ideas.

units.why: The sample statement lists "Fine tuning your research questions" among the uses permitted in the course, a brainstorming-type use like the neighbouring items, so P15, may, student, during-work.
units.anchor: Fine tuning your research questions
units.policy: The use of generative AI tools is permitted in this course for fine tuning your research questions.
units.resolution_why: Neither coder coded this list item, although both coded its siblings ('Brainstorming and refining your ideas', 'Finding information on your topic'). It is in the source as one of the permitted uses, so the reconciler added it and coded it like its neighbours under P15.

units.why: The sample statement permits "Finding information on your topic" with AI, like using a search engine to learn about a subject, so P12 fits better than P15.
units.anchor: Finding information on your topic
units.policy: The use of generative AI tools is permitted in this course for finding information on your topic.

units.why: The sample statement permits "Drafting an outline to organize your thoughts", a writing-support use, so P91 (editing and writing support) fits rather than P15.
units.anchor: Drafting an outline to organize your thoughts
units.policy: The use of generative AI tools is permitted in this course for drafting an outline to organize your thoughts.

units.why: The sample statement permits "Checking grammar and style", which is proofreading support, so P91.
units.anchor: Checking grammar and style
units.policy: The use of generative AI tools is permitted in this course for checking grammar and style.

units.why: The sample statement forbids "Impersonating you in classroom contexts" such as composing discussion board replies or chat content, which is AI-written course communication, so P58.
units.anchor: Impersonating you in classroom contexts
units.policy: The use of generative AI tools is not permitted in this course for impersonating you in classroom contexts, such as composing discussion board replies or content that you put into a Teams or Zoom chat.
units.fit_note: Covers discussion board replies and Teams or Zoom chat content, not only messages to course staff. Also covers chat content in Teams or Zoom, not only messages to staff.

units.why: The sample statement forbids "Completing group work that your group has assigned to you" with AI unless the group agrees; this is AI producing the student's own share of submitted work, so P19, with a note on the group-consent exception.
units.anchor: Completing group work that your group has assigned to you
units.policy: The use of generative AI tools is not permitted in this course for completing group work that your group has assigned to you, unless it is mutually agreed upon that you may utilize the tool.
units.fit_note: Allows an exception when the group mutually agrees to use the tool.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on policy_type: A P19, B UNCOVERED. A: P19 with a fit note on the group-agreement exception; B: UNCOVERED, 'AI may not do a student's assigned share of group work unless the group agrees'. The source bars AI from 'Completing group work that your group has assigned to you', which is AI producing the part of the submitted work the student owns, the definition of P19; the exception is a qualifier, not a different kind of rule. Final: P19 with A's fit note. (B's uncovered_note kept here: AI may not do a student's assigned share of group work unless the group agrees.) Final: actor student, phase during-work, modality must-not, policy_type P19, unit_stance restrict. (Coder B's uncovered_note: AI may not do a student's assigned share of group work unless the group agrees.)

units.why: The sample statement forbids "Writing a draft of a writing assignment" with AI; a draft is work submitted as one's own, so P19.
units.anchor: Writing a draft of a writing assignment
units.policy: The use of generative AI tools is not permitted in this course for writing a draft of a writing assignment.

units.why: The sample statement forbids "Writing entire sentences, paragraphs, or papers to complete class assignments", AI-produced submitted text, so P19.
units.anchor: Writing entire sentences, paragraphs, or papers to complete class assignments
units.policy: The use of generative AI tools is not permitted in this course for writing entire sentences, paragraphs, or papers to complete class assignments.

units.why: The "For instructors who wish to embrace AI" template says AI "is permitted in this course for students who wish to use them", a default-permit rule, so P02.
units.anchor: is permitted in this course for students who wish to use them
units.frag_start: The use of AI tools, including
units.policy: The use of AI tools, including ChatGPT, is permitted in this course for students who wish to use them.

units.why: The template tells students "You are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query" (IP, misinformation, unethical content), which makes students own what they submit, so P29; verification (P31) is not stated explicitly.
units.anchor: You are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query
units.policy: You are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query, for instance that it does not violate intellectual property laws or contain misinformation or unethical content.
units.fit_note: Also names IP violations, misinformation and unethical content as risks.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance: A neutral, B require. Only the unit stance differed (A neutral, B require). The sentence makes students answerable for what they submit; it takes no position on whether AI is used, so neutral. Final: actor student, phase during-work, modality must, policy_type P29, unit_stance neutral.

units.why: The template requires that AI use "must be properly documented and cited" to stay within academic honesty policy, a disclosure-with-submission rule, so P24.
units.anchor: Your use of AI tools must be properly documented and cited
units.policy: Your use of AI tools must be properly documented and cited, using quotation marks or other appropriate indicators of quoted material when appropriate, in order to stay within university policies on academic honesty.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance: A permit, B require. Only the unit stance differed (A permit, B require). The statement sits in a template that permits AI and attaches a documentation condition, so the position on AI use is permit (conditional). Final: actor student, phase during-work, modality must, policy_type P24, unit_stance permit.

units.why: The limited-use template permits AI "for specific assignments only" and says allowed use "will be explicitly noted in the assignment directions", so the decision is made per assignment: P04 is the best fit over P09.
units.anchor: permitted in this course for specific assignments only
units.policy: The use of AI tools, including ChatGPT, is permitted in this course for specific assignments only, and when use of the tool is allowed it is explicitly noted in the assignment directions.
units.fit_note: Also sets a restrictive default: AI is allowed only where an assignment says so.

units.why: "it will be explicitly noted in the assignment directions" requires the assignment to state when AI is allowed: P09.
units.anchor: it will be explicitly noted in the assignment directions
units.frag_start: When the use of the tool is allowed
units.policy: When the use of the tool is allowed, it will be explicitly noted in the assignment directions.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this. 'it will be explicitly noted in the assignment directions' is a separate rule from 'permitted ... for specific assignments only': assignments must say when AI is allowed. A had merged both into one P04 unit. Kept as its own unit; P09 is the nearest type but concerns the syllabus, so B's fit note is kept.

units.why: The page advises "creating alternative learning pathways for students who do not want to use AI tools" when AI is required, which provides an equitable alternative, so P51.
units.anchor: alternative learning pathways for students who do not want to use AI tools
units.policy: Instructors who require students to use AI tools for all or certain assignments consider creating alternative learning pathways, with the same learning outcomes, for students who do not want to use AI tools.
units.fit_note: Concerns instructors who require AI use; alternatives keep the same learning outcomes.

units.why: The page recommends "transparently communicating to students before or at the start of the semester that they will be expected to use AI", a communication-of-expectations rule, so P09 as nearest, noting it is specific to AI-required courses.
units.anchor: transparently communicating to students before or at the start of the semester
units.policy: If using AI tools is essential to the learning outcomes, instructors transparently communicate to students before or at the start of the semester that they will be expected to use AI in the course.
units.fit_note: Applies only to courses where AI use is essential to learning outcomes, and speaks of communication before or at the start of the semester rather than a syllabus statement. Specifically about courses that require AI use, so students can decide whether to stay.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance: A require, B neutral. Only the unit stance differed (A require, B neutral). The rule is about telling students in advance; it does not itself require AI use, so neutral. Final: actor instructor, phase course-start, modality should, policy_type P09, unit_stance neutral.

units.why: "The Faculty Resource Center does not recommend this" about prohibiting AI advises instructors against a ban without forbidding one and without saying AI is allowed by default; no type states that, so UNCOVERED rather than a stretch to P02.
units.anchor: The Faculty Resource Center does not recommend this.
units.policy: The Faculty Resource Center does not recommend prohibiting the use of AI.
units.uncovered_note: The FRC advises instructors against prohibiting AI use in their courses.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on policy_type: A P02, B UNCOVERED; unit_stance: A permit, B encourage. A: P02 with a fit note ('advice against banning AI, not a default rule that AI is allowed'); B: UNCOVERED. P02 is a default rule that AI is allowed or encouraged; the source only says the FRC does not recommend a ban, so P02 is a stretch and the codebook prefers UNCOVERED. The stance toward AI is permit (it argues against banning), not encourage. Final: actor instructor, phase before-course, modality should-not, policy_type UNCOVERED, unit_stance permit. (Coder A's fit_note on P02: It is advice against banning AI, not a default rule that AI is allowed.)

units.why: The reason given for not prohibiting AI is that "students will likely be expected to use AI in the workplace" and should be taught to use it responsibly, a career-skill rationale, so P44.
units.anchor: students will likely be expected to use AI in the workplace when they graduate
units.policy: Students will likely be expected to use AI in the workplace when they graduate, and we should be teaching them how to use it responsibly and ethically.

units.why: The page says "there are currently no tools that can accurately detect AI writing" and that false positives "could lead to false allegations", which is an argument not to rely on detectors, so P39.
units.anchor: there are currently no tools that can accurately detect AI writing
units.policy: There are currently no tools that can accurately detect AI writing; all available tools generate too many false positives that could lead to false allegations.

units.why: The page invites instructors to "contact the FRC for a consultation" on discerning acceptable AI use, which is faculty support, so P63.
units.anchor: contact the FRC for a consultation
units.policy: Instructors can contact the Faculty Resource Center for a consultation on a more holistic approach to discerning acceptable use of AI-generated assignments.

units.why: The page tells faculty to "Prepare yourself and your students for the ChatGPT EDU rollout", pointing to a university-licensed tool for the whole campus, so P92 rather than P17 (which is course-specific).
units.anchor: Prepare yourself and your students for the
units.policy: Faculty prepare themselves and their students for the ChatGPT EDU rollout.
units.fit_note: The text announces a rollout rather than stating a use rule.

units.why: The scale defines "The 5 Levels of AI-Integrated Assessment" (No AI, AI Planning, AI Collaboration, Full AI, AI Exploration), named levels of permitted AI use per assignment, so P05.
units.anchor: The 5 Levels of AI-Integrated Assessment
units.policy: The university's Faculty Resource Center offers a five-level AI-Integrated Assessment Scale: 1 No AI, 2 AI Planning, 3 AI Collaboration, 4 Full AI, 5 AI Exploration.

units.why: Level 1 says "You must not use AI at any point during the activity/assignment/ assessment", a ban for work done in a controlled environment, so P22 with a note that it also covers assignments.
units.anchor: You must not use AI at any point during the activity/assignment/ assessment.
units.frag_start: You must not use AI at any point
units.policy: At Level 1 (No AI), you must not use AI at any point during the activity, assignment or assessment.
units.fit_note: Covers activities and assignments as well as assessments. Applies to activities and assignments as well as assessments, completed in a controlled environment.

units.why: Level 1 strategy: "Conduct such activities in class or using Respondus and Lock-down browser" moves No-AI work to supervised settings, so P33.
units.anchor: Conduct such activities in class or using
units.frag_start: Conduct such activities in class or
units.policy: At Level 1, conduct such activities in class or using Respondus and Lock-down browser.
units.fit_note: Does not say weight shifts overall; it names in-class or lockdown-browser delivery for No-AI activities.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance: A restrict, B neutral. Only the unit stance differed (A restrict, B neutral). The strategy exists to enforce Level 1 'No AI' by moving the work to supervised settings, so it restricts AI use. Final: actor instructor, phase during-assessment, modality should, policy_type P33, unit_stance restrict.

units.why: The Level 1 strategy "Make the activity/assignment/assessment one that can be completed with peers or open resources" tells instructors how to design No-AI work, an AI-resistant redesign of the task, so P35.
units.anchor: can be completed with peers or open resources
units.policy: At Level 1, make the activity, assignment or assessment one that can be completed with peers or open resources (physical notes, textbook, other supplemental material).
units.resolution_why: Neither coder coded this Level 1 strategy, although both coded the other Level 1 strategies. It is in the source (line under 'Associated AI-Resistant Strategies'), so the reconciler added it; P35 fits as a redesign of the task around the No-AI rule.

units.why: Level 1 strategy: "Have students produce a physical artifact and explain it orally or through a personal reflection" checks understanding by explanation, so P34.
units.anchor: Have students produce a physical artifact and explain it orally
units.policy: At Level 1, have students produce a physical artifact and explain it orally or through a personal reflection.

units.why: Level 1 strategy: "Focus on assessing the process" by outlining steps, justifying decisions and reflecting, redesigns the assessment around process rather than product, so P35.
units.anchor: Focus on assessing the process by asking students to outline the steps they take
units.policy: At Level 1, focus on assessing the process by asking students to outline the steps they take, explain and justify their decision-making process, and reflect on how completing the work enhanced their knowledge, skills, or experience.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on phase: A during-work, B before-course. Only the phase differed (A during-work, B before-course). The sentence is advice to instructors on how to design the assessment, so before-course. Final: actor instructor, phase before-course, modality should, policy_type P35, unit_stance neutral.

units.why: Level 1 strategy "Anchor the activity... in a local entity context that requires details AI may not have access to" is an AI-resistant task design, so P35.
units.anchor: Anchor the activity/assignment/assessment in a local entity context
units.policy: At Level 1, anchor the activity, assignment or assessment in a local entity context that requires details AI may not have access to.

units.why: The line "Include adherence to the AI scale level as a part of the grading rubric" (repeated at every level) grades compliance with the AI level, a grading redesign, so P35.
units.anchor: Include adherence to the AI scale level as a part of the grading rubric.
units.policy: At every level, include adherence to the AI scale level as a part of the grading rubric.
units.fit_note: Repeated under every level; coded once.

units.why: Level 2 tells students "You may use AI for planning, idea development, and research", a brainstorming-type permission, so P15.
units.anchor: You may use AI for planning, idea development, and research.
units.frag_start: You may use AI for planning
units.policy: At Level 2 (AI Planning), you may use AI for planning, idea development, and research.

units.why: Level 2 adds "Your final submission should show how you have developed and refined these ideas", keeping the student the developer of the work, so P32.
units.anchor: Your final submission should show how you have developed and refined these ideas.
units.policy: At Level 2, your final submission should show how you have developed and refined these ideas.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance: A permit, B require. Only the unit stance differed (A permit, B require). The sentence conditions permitted Level 2 use on the final submission showing the student's own development, so permit. Final: actor student, phase during-work, modality should, policy_type P32, unit_stance permit.

units.why: The strategy "Define and provide access to the OIT permitted AI tool(s)" has instructors name and supply sanctioned tools, so P17 (repeated across Levels 2 to 5).
units.anchor: Define and provide access to the
units.frag_start: Define and provide access to the
units.policy: At Levels 2 to 5, instructors define and provide access to the OIT permitted AI tool(s) students are permitted to use for the activity or assignment.
units.fit_note: Listed under levels 2 to 5; coded once.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance: A permit, B neutral. Only the unit stance differed (A permit, B neutral). The strategy is attached to Levels 2 to 5, where AI is allowed, and supplies the sanctioned tool, so permit. Final: actor instructor, phase before-course, modality should, policy_type P17, unit_stance permit.

units.why: The strategy "Work with students to develop an ethics-based use policy" has instructors build the rules together with students, so P67.
units.anchor: Work with students to develop an ethics-based use policy.
units.policy: At Levels 2 to 5, instructors work with students to develop an ethics-based use policy.
units.fit_note: Listed under levels 2 to 5; coded once.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on phase: A course-start, B before-course; unit_stance: A neutral, B encourage. A: course-start and neutral; B: before-course and encourage. Developing a use policy 'with students' happens once students are in the course, so course-start. The sentence is a procedure and takes no position on AI itself, so neutral. Final: actor instructor, phase course-start, modality should, policy_type P67, unit_stance neutral.

units.why: The strategy to "Demonstrate and have students practice using the permitted tools in the way they are being asked to use them" has instructors teach AI use, so P44.
units.anchor: Demonstrate and have students practice using the permitted tools
units.policy: At Levels 2 to 5, instructors demonstrate the permitted tools and have students practice using them in the way they are being asked to use them.
units.fit_note: Teaching the specific permitted use of a tool within an assignment, not a general professional-skill claim. Instruction in the permitted tools, not an employer-skills argument.

units.why: The strategy "Have students capture their use of the AI tool through screenshots, process steps, and/or a summary" asks for records of AI use, so P26.
units.anchor: Have students capture their use of the AI tool through screenshots, process steps
units.policy: At Levels 2 to 5, instructors have students capture their use of the AI tool through screenshots, process steps, and/or a summary, including an explanation of how they upheld the ethics-based use policy.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance: A permit, B require. Only the unit stance differed (A permit, B require). Capturing a record is a condition on permitted use at Levels 2 to 5, so permit. Final: actor instructor, phase during-work, modality should, policy_type P26, unit_stance permit.

units.why: Level 3 lets students "use AI to assist with specific tasks such as drafting text, refining, and evaluating your work", writing-support use, so P91, with a note that it includes drafting.
units.anchor: You may use AI to assist with specific tasks such as drafting text
units.frag_start: You may use AI to assist with
units.policy: At Level 3 (AI Collaboration), you may use AI to assist with specific tasks such as drafting text, refining, and evaluating your work.
units.fit_note: Includes drafting text, not only editing or proofreading. Includes drafting text, which goes beyond editing.

units.why: Level 3 adds "You must critically evaluate and modify any AI-generated content you use", a duty to evaluate output, so P31.
units.anchor: You must critically evaluate and modify any AI-generated content you use.
units.policy: At Level 3, you must critically evaluate and modify any AI-generated content you use.
units.fit_note: Also requires modifying the content, not only verifying it.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance: A permit, B require. Only the unit stance differed (A permit, B require). At Level 3 AI use is allowed and the student must evaluate and modify the output; the position on AI is permit with a condition. Final: actor student, phase during-work, modality must, policy_type P31, unit_stance permit.

units.why: Level 4 says "You may use AI extensively throughout your work either as you wish, or as specifically directed", an open-use rule, so P02.
units.anchor: You may use AI extensively throughout your work
units.frag_start: You may use AI extensively throughout
units.policy: At Level 4 (Full AI), you may use AI extensively throughout your work either as you wish, or as specifically directed in your assessment.

units.why: Level 4 notes assessments "may also require engagement with AI to achieve goals and solve problems", so AI use is built into the task: P79.
units.anchor: Assessments at this level may also require engagement with AI
units.policy: Assessments at Level 4 may also require engagement with AI to achieve goals and solve problems.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded this. Level 4 says 'Assessments at this level may also require engagement with AI to achieve goals and solve problems', which says assessments may require AI use (P79). It is in the source, so kept.

units.why: Level 4 asks students to "Focus on directing AI to achieve your goals while demonstrating your critical thinking", keeping the student as decision-maker, so P32.
units.anchor: Focus on directing AI to achieve your goals while demonstrating your critical thinking.
units.policy: At Level 4, focus on directing AI to achieve your goals while demonstrating your critical thinking.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance: A permit, B encourage. Only the unit stance differed (A permit, B encourage). 'Focus on directing AI to achieve your goals while demonstrating your critical thinking' is a condition on allowed Level 4 use, not a push to use more AI, so permit. Final: actor student, phase during-work, modality should, policy_type P32, unit_stance permit.

units.why: Level 5 says "You should use AI creatively to solve the task, potentially co-designing new approaches with your instructor", which encourages AI use, so P02.
units.anchor: You should use AI creatively to solve the task
units.frag_start: You should use AI creatively to solve
units.policy: At Level 5 (AI Exploration), you should use AI creatively to solve the task, potentially co-designing new approaches with your instructor.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on policy_type: A P02, B P79; unit_stance: A encourage, B require. A: P02 and encourage; B: P79 (require AI use) and require. The wording is 'You should use AI creatively', which welcomes and expects use at this level but does not make it a graded requirement (compare Level 4 'may ... either as you wish'); the modality is should, so P02 (permit or encourage) fits and the stance is encourage, not require. Final: actor student, phase during-work, modality should, policy_type P02, unit_stance encourage.

units.why: "Students and educators co-design assessments to explore unique AI applications" redesigns assessment around AI: P35.
units.anchor: Students and educators co-design assessments
units.fit_note: Co-designing assessments with students rather than a fixed redesign.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this. 'Students and educators co-design assessments to explore unique AI applications' is in the Level 5 description and is a real statement of how assessment is designed at that level (P35). Kept; B's fit note kept.

units.why: Level 5 says the capture of AI use "should include a reflection about the impact the collaboration made on the final product", a reflection requirement, so P26.
units.anchor: a reflection about the impact the collaboration made on the final product
units.policy: At Level 5, the student's record of AI use includes a reflection about the impact the collaboration made on the final product.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance: A encourage, B require. A: encourage; B: require. The reflection is part of the record students keep when they use AI at Level 5; it conditions the use rather than pushing it, so permit. Final: actor student, phase during-work, modality should, policy_type P26, unit_stance permit.

units.why: The Canvas instructions have instructors "select the indicator of choice" and place an AI indicator on each assignment, which communicates the level to students; P09 is nearest but it is about syllabus statements, so a fit note is added.
units.anchor: Expand the AI indicator menu and select the indicator of choice.
units.policy: Instructors place an AI indicator on an assignment in Canvas by expanding the AI indicator menu and selecting the indicator of choice.
units.fit_note: Communicates the AI level on each assignment page in Canvas, not in the syllabus. Describes a Canvas template mechanism; placement is a recommended step, not mandated.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on phase: A before-course, B course-start. Only the phase differed (A before-course, B course-start). Placing the indicator happens when the instructor builds the assignment ('Create a new assignment'), so before-course. Final: actor instructor, phase before-course, modality should, policy_type P09, unit_stance neutral.

units.why: The page offers support to "schedule an appointment with Angie Dodson for assistance" in setting up the AI indicators, which is faculty support, so P63.
units.anchor: with Angie Dodson for assistance with this process.
units.policy: Instructors can schedule an appointment with Angie Dodson, FRC Faculty Development Coordinator, for assistance with placing AI indicators in Canvas.
units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded this. The sentence 'Please schedule an appointment with Angie Dodson for assistance with this process' offers faculty support in setting up AI indicators (P63). It is in the source, so kept.

units.why: The resources list links an instructional plan titled "Establishing Ethical an Acceptable AI Use Policy with Students", which promotes setting the rules with students: P67.
units.anchor: Establishing Ethical an Acceptable AI Use Policy with Students
units.policy: The Faculty Resource Center lists an instructional plan on establishing an ethical and acceptable AI use policy with students.
units.fit_note: Only a resource title; the plan itself is not in the text.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on modality: A informs, B should; unit_stance: A neutral, B encourage. A: informs and neutral; B: should and encourage. The resource list only names an instructional plan; it does not tell instructors to do anything, so informs and neutral. Final: actor instructor, phase before-course, modality informs, policy_type P67, unit_stance neutral.

documents.title: Artificial intelligence (AI) at UCCS
documents.summary: The page tells students to use AI to support learning and not as a shortcut, to disclose and document use, and to verify output. It leaves whether AI is allowed to each course syllabus.
documents.stance_why: The page gives student-facing expectations about learning, transparency and ethics, and leaves whether AI is allowed to each course syllabus ("faculty set their own course-level AI policies"), so the document stance is delegates.

units.why: The page hopes students use AI "to support and enhance your education" and "not as a shortcut that will interfere with your learning"; this discourages shortcut use without forbidding it, which is P03. The explanation of why shortcuts hurt is the next sentence (P41).
units.anchor: not as a shortcut that will interfere with your learning
units.policy: We hope you use AI at UCCS to support and enhance your education, not as a shortcut that will interfere with your learning.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on policy_type: A P41, B P03; unit_stance: A neutral, B restrict. A: P41 (explain that shortcuts undercut practice), neutral; B: P03 (discourage without forbidding), restrict. This sentence states a hope about how students use AI, which is discouragement; the explanation that shortcuts undercut learning is the following sentence, which both coders coded as P41. Final P03 and restrict. Final: actor student, phase general, modality should, policy_type P03, unit_stance restrict.

units.why: The page warns that "reliance on AI tools to produce essays, presentations, lab reports... means you aren’t building new skills", the practice-shortcut rationale, so P41.
units.anchor: you aren’t building new skills, practicing new ways of thinking
units.policy: Relying on AI tools to produce essays, presentations, lab reports, artwork, and podcasts means students aren't building new skills, practicing new ways of thinking, or developing a strong work ethic.

units.why: It says that when AI is a shortcut "you won’t learn as much and will be less prepared for your future career"; this cites careers as the reason to build skills without AI, so P94 rather than P41.
units.anchor: you won’t learn as much and will be less prepared for your future career
units.policy: When Gen AI is used as a shortcut to the outcome, students won't learn as much and will be less prepared for their future career.

units.why: The sentence defines generative AI: "these systems are called 'large language models' (LLMs)", an explanation of what is covered, so P61.
units.anchor: these systems are called “large language models” (LLMs)
units.policy: Generative AI involves algorithms that enable machine learning from enormous data sets; these systems are called large language models (LLMs).
units.fit_note: An explanatory description of how generative AI works rather than a scope definition for a policy.

units.why: The "Prompting 101" text says "Asking good, specific questions and iterating with the tool as you work will maximize its effectiveness", which is prompting advice, so P93.
units.anchor: Asking good, specific questions and iterating with the tool as you work
units.policy: Asking good, specific questions and iterating with the tool as you work will maximize its effectiveness.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance: A neutral, B encourage. Only the unit stance differed (A neutral, B encourage). Prompting advice takes no position on whether AI may be used, so neutral. Final: actor student, phase during-work, modality should, policy_type P93, unit_stance neutral.

units.why: The page says "Always be transparent about how you’ve used AI and document your use appropriately", a general disclosure duty, so P24.
units.anchor: Always be transparent about how you’ve used AI and document your use appropriately.
units.policy: Always be transparent about how you've used AI and document your use appropriately.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on modality: A should, B must; unit_stance: A permit, B require. A: should and permit; B: must and require. The sentence is an imperative ('Always be transparent ... and document your use'), so must; the next sentence calls an AI Use statement 'a good practice', which is the should-level one. The position on AI use is permit with a disclosure condition. Final: actor student, phase during-work, modality must, policy_type P24, unit_stance permit.

units.why: It recommends an "AI Use" statement "that details what AI tools you used and how you used them", which names the tool and the manner of use, so P25 rather than the general P24 above.
units.anchor: An “AI Use” statement at the end of your project
units.policy: An 'AI Use' statement at the end of your project that details what AI tools you used and how you used them is a good practice.

units.why: It tells students to "ask your teacher if you have questions about how to document AI use in a specific class", which is ask-first advice, so P10 with a note that it concerns documentation.
units.anchor: ask your teacher if you have questions about how to document AI use
units.policy: You should ask your teacher if you have questions about how to document AI use in a specific class.
units.fit_note: The question to ask concerns how to document AI use, not whether a use is allowed. Asks about how to document, not whether use is allowed.

units.why: The sentence "faculty set their own course-level AI policies" hands the decision to instructors, so P04.
units.anchor: faculty set their own course-level AI policies
units.policy: Faculty set their own course-level AI policies.

units.why: The page tells students "it's important to follow the policy outlined in the course syllabus" because faculty rules differ, so P78.
units.anchor: it's important to follow the policy outlined in the course syllabus
units.policy: Students follow the AI policy outlined in the course syllabus, because some faculty may encourage AI use for parts of the work while others may consider any use to be academic dishonesty.

units.why: "others may consider any use to be academic dishonesty" warns that some courses treat any AI use as misconduct: P36.
units.anchor: others may consider any use to be academic dishonesty
units.frag_start: Some faculty may encourage AI use
units.fit_note: States that policies range from encouraging to treating any use as dishonesty.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this. 'others may consider any use to be academic dishonesty' states that some courses treat any AI use as misconduct, which is a real statement on integrity rules (P36). A had folded it into the P78 unit's policy text; it is a distinct statement so it is kept as its own unit. It informs, since it describes what some faculty do.

units.why: The page warns that "many AI tools require paid subscriptions for unlimited use or to access all of their features", a note on cost to students, so P51 in part. It does not say paid tools may not be required; the advice to research tools is coded as a separate unit.
units.anchor: many AI tools require paid subscriptions for unlimited use
units.policy: Many AI tools require paid subscriptions for unlimited use or to access all of their features.
units.fit_note: States the cost of AI tools but does not say paid tools are not required.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on phase: A during-work, B before-course; modality: A informs, B should. A joined the cost note and the advice to research tools in one unit (informs, during-work); B anchored on the advice to research (should, before-course). They are two rules, so this unit keeps only the cost note (informs, general) and the advice to research tools is a separate unit. Final: actor student, phase general, modality informs, policy_type P51, unit_stance neutral.

units.why: The page advises "Research tools before deciding to use them for a class or assignment", advice to look into a tool (including its cost) before choosing it; this is not prompting advice (P93) and not an access rule (P51), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Research tools before deciding to use them for a class or assignment.
units.uncovered_note: Students should research an AI tool before deciding to use it for a class or assignment.
units.resolution_why: Split from the cost note. Coder A joined the cost note and this advice in one P51 unit; coder B anchored on this sentence (P51 in part, should, before-course, with a fit note: 'Advises students to research cost before use; does not forbid requiring paid tools'). The advice to research a tool before choosing it is a separate rule and no type covers it, so it is UNCOVERED; the phase is during-work because the student is choosing a tool for an assignment.

units.why: It states "You have free access to some AI tools as a UCCS student" and discounts for others, which is access provision, so P51.
units.anchor: You have free access to some AI tools as a UCCS student.
units.policy: UCCS students have free access to some AI tools and can get a student discount for others.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance: A encourage, B neutral. Only the unit stance differed (A encourage, B neutral). The sentence reports that free and discounted tools exist and does not urge their use, so neutral. Final: actor student, phase general, modality informs, policy_type P51, unit_stance neutral.

units.why: It points students to the Kraemer Family Library, which "has more guidance for students around AI and Research", a support unit, so P72.
units.anchor: Kramer Family Library has more guidance for students around AI and Research
units.policy: UCCS's Kraemer Family Library has more guidance for students around AI and research, including an overview of tools for specific research tasks.
units.fit_note: Directs students to library guidance on AI research tools rather than to a person. Points to library web guidance, not directly to a librarian.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on phase: A during-work, B general. Only the phase differed (A during-work, B general). The sentence points to a resource and is not tied to a stage of the work, so general. Final: actor student, phase general, modality informs, policy_type P72, unit_stance neutral.

units.why: "choose a tool that's designed for that kind of work" advises matching the AI tool to the task. P93 is about writing prompts, and no other type covers choosing a tool, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: choose a tool that’s designed for that kind of work
units.policy: Students understand what they need to do and choose an AI tool that is designed for that kind of work.
units.uncovered_note: Students should choose an AI tool suited to the type of task.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on policy_type: A P93, B UNCOVERED. A: P93 with a fit note ('advice on choosing a tool for a task rather than on writing prompts'); B: UNCOVERED. P93 is 'advise on how to prompt AI effectively'; picking a tool is a different kind of advice, and the codebook prefers UNCOVERED to a stretched fit. Final: actor student, phase during-work, modality should, policy_type UNCOVERED, unit_stance neutral. (Coder A's fit_note on P93: Advice on choosing a tool for a task rather than on writing prompts.)

units.why: "it’s likely the output will also be biased" describes bias in AI output: P53.
units.anchor: it’s likely the output will also be biased.
units.frag_start: The output AI provides is only as good
units.frag_end: generate a picture of a doctor
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this. 'it's likely the output will also be biased' states a harm of biased AI output (P53). A coded only the follow-up duty to evaluate for bias. Both are real statements, so it is kept.

units.why: It says "it’s important to evaluate AI output with special attention to bias", an output-checking duty, so P31.
units.anchor: it’s important to evaluate AI output with special attention to bias
units.policy: Because AI tools often pull from biased data, students evaluate AI output with special attention to bias.

units.why: It says "It is your responsibility to confirm the information produced by a generative AI" and verify cited sources exist, so P31.
units.anchor: It is your responsibility to confirm the information produced by a generative AI
units.policy: It is your responsibility to confirm the information produced by a generative AI by locating additional sources of information and to verify the existence of any book or article it claims to cite.
units.fit_note: Also requires verifying that cited books or articles exist.
units.resolution_why: Coders differed on unit_stance: A neutral, B require. Only the unit stance differed (A neutral, B require). The sentence makes students responsible for checking output; it takes no position on whether AI may be used, so neutral. Final: actor student, phase during-work, modality must, policy_type P31, unit_stance neutral.

units.why: It says "Every time you use AI, there is an environmental cost. Be cognizant of that cost", an environmental concern, so P53.
units.anchor: Be cognizant of that cost as you weigh when and how you’ll use AI
units.policy: Every time you use AI there is an environmental cost; be cognizant of that cost as you weigh when and how you'll use AI now and in the future.

units.why: Lawsuits alleging generative AI was "trained on the work of authors" without permission raise copyright concerns: P52.
units.anchor: trained on the work of authors, journalists, artists, or musicians
units.frag_start: Some generative AIs were trained on
units.resolution_why: Only coder B coded this. The sentence that some generative AIs 'were trained on the work of authors ... who did not give the companies permission' and the resulting lawsuits states a copyright concern (P52). A coded only the 'consider the ethical implications' sentence. Kept.

units.why: It asks students to "consider the ethical implications of uploading another author or artist’s work" to AI, a copyright concern, so P52 (not P49, which is about course materials).
units.anchor: consider the ethical implications of uploading another author or artist’s work
units.policy: When using generative AI tools, consider the ethical implications of uploading another author or artist's work or prompting the AI to produce outputs based on copyrighted characters.
units.fit_note: Frames copyright as an ethical consideration, not a legal rule or permission. Asks for consideration, not a ban on uploading protected works.

notes: Reconciled from coder A (63 units) and coder B (67 units): 60 matched, 3 only A (2 kept, 1 dropped), 7 only B (all kept). The reconciler added 2 list-item or strategy units that neither coder coded ('Fine tuning your research questions' and the Level 1 open-resources strategy) and split one merged P51 unit into a cost note and a separate research-tools advice unit (UNCOVERED). Repeated AI-resistant strategies at Levels 2 to 5 and the repeated rubric line are coded once, as both coders did. Reference lists, navigation and links are not coded. Course layer deferred; no school or computing policy found. CU system policy APS 6012 is under colorado-boulder per collect notes. Recurring UNCOVERED items for the codebook review: (1) advice to choose or research an AI tool before use, (2) advice against prohibiting AI. Coder notes carried over: A: anchors that fall mid-sentence were given full-sentence frag_start and frag_end; B: sentences repeated across levels coded once.
